acceptance: A cancelled CI run no longer delays the next run for the same PR waiting on its summary jobs; shown on a PR with two quick pushes while the pool is busy, or by run timing over 7 days
Required contexts on the live head still report the real outcome; a cancelled run never posts success for a head that did not pass (tests on the summary-job conditions)
The workflow dedupe test fails when a workflow sets both push and pull_request branches to ['**']
context: Source: CI cost study on ci-duplicate-dispatch-ghost-runs (2026-10-25), approved by the owner.
description: When a push cancels a CI run, that run's 5 required summary jobs (core, explorer, results-data, docs, tooling) still run because they use `if: always()`. When the 20-job runner pool is full they wait for a slot, and the new run for the same PR gets no jobs until they finish, because of per-PR concurrency. Seen 22 times from 2026-10-11 to 10-25: median 26 min, max 177 min (run 39803982201: summary jobs started about 3 h late, and the next run got its first job the second they finished). Make a superseded run's summary jobs skip or finish without a runner wait while keeping required contexts correct for the live head. Also extend the #3434 dedupe test to catch `push` and `pull_request` both set to `['**']`.
